revision_history: v1 (2026-09-19): initial draft after Phase 1 brief approval. Companion to issue 2014; linked only if Sherlock's shared-entity rule fires. Frame: every Malaysian security instrument on the Thai border is switched on while the one diplomatic instrument only Putrajaya controls, the facilitator's chair, has been vacant since the summer. Anchor: anger-at-process (a 'soon' with no date). Lessons carried from 2014's reviews: bounded claims, attributed counts, 'rangers' not 'soldiers', no inference beyond the record on sanctuary.
_provenance.discipline: Neither attack is attributed to the BRN (ACLED: too early; no claim of responsibility; the BRN spokesman neither confirmed nor denied). The BRN delegation in Kuala Lumpur is described as the negotiating party Thailand asked Malaysia to host. Both official reasons for the suspension (the 22 July attack; the facilitator transition) run attributed. Rabin's exact end date and contract term are not stated because they are not published. Nikmatullah's governance proposals stay off the cards. No AI-provider name and no 'AI' appears on any card.

headline: Thailand suspended BRN talks on 28 July. Malaysia has had no facilitator since the summer.
context: Malaysia has facilitated the Thailand-BRN dialogue since 2013. A 22 July attack killed five rangers and Bangkok cancelled September's round. Rabin Basir's facilitator contract then expired; on 27 August Khaled said names were with the PM. No appointment as of 19 September.

cards.big: Bangkok cancelled September's Kuala Lumpur round on 28 July: 'The violence was too severe for us to accept.' By 27 August Malaysia's facilitator seat was empty too.
cards.sub: The BRN's negotiator, in a KL hotel on 14 September: the talks were 'hampered by the absence of a Malaysian mediator'.

cards.big: Six masked attackers killed five rangers at Rangae's Bukit Sami checkpoint on 22 July. Six days later Thanat Suwannanont called off the September round.
cards.sub: On 31 July Thailand's NSC cited 'the transition to a new facilitator'. Seventeen days earlier Khaled had said Rabin Basir 'will continue his role'.

cards.big: Fifty-one attacks in four hours on 22 August, by ISOC's count. Blasts shook Rantau Panjang; inbound crossings fell from 2,068 that Saturday to 1,230 in two days.
cards.sub: PDRM agreed on 26 August to trace BRN-linked individuals for Thailand. Army chief Azhan Md Othman put drones on the border on 17 September: 'no compromise'.

cards.big: Khaled confirmed on 27 August that Rabin Basir's contract had expired and the Armed Forces had sent names to Anwar. On 18 September he told AFP: 'under consideration'.
cards.sub: Rabin was appointed 1 July 2024. Sihasak on 7 September: the choice 'was ultimately Malaysia's decision'. Malaysia has facilitated since 2013.

cards.big: Malaysia is doing everything on this border except the one thing Thailand asked it to do.
Like a host who locks every door, posts guards at the gate, and never sets a chair at the table.
Drones watch the border. Police trace names for Bangkok. The chair that hosts the talks sits empty; Putrajaya has said 'soon' for three weeks. Name the facilitator or the date.

confidence: High on every dated statement (Bernama carrying MKN, IGP, Defence Minister, Army chief; Thai NSC via Bernama; AFP). High on the 51 count (ISOC final, carried by AFP/Reuters and ACLED; preliminary 25 and 34 noted in the brief). Medium on the facilitator timeline: the end date and term of Rabin's contract are unpublished, so the cards say 'expired' and 'since the summer' without a date. Medium on 'for three weeks': the 27 August 'soon' to 19 September is three weeks and two days.
needs_verification: 'Six masked attackers': Bernama 28 Jul says 'six masked assailants'; the Washington Post wire said 'about 10 assailants'. Bernama's figure is used; Stage 3 to confirm against Thai ISOC statements.
'Five rangers': Bernama and The Nation say paramilitary rangers (thahan phran); AFP says 'five soldiers'. Rangers used throughout.
'The transition to a new facilitator': Thai NSC secretary-general Chatchai's statement as carried by Bernama on 31 Jul; Thai-language original not opened.
'Inbound crossings fell from 2,068 that Saturday to 1,230 over the next two days': AKPS Rantau Panjang commander via Bernama; the 1,230 is Sunday and Monday combined, as the card says.

'Putrajaya has said soon for three weeks': 'soon' is Malay Mail/Yahoo's report of Khaled on 27 Aug ('expected to appoint the facilitators soon'); Bernama's version has 'hope a facilitator can be appointed'. The 18 Sep 'under consideration' is Khaled's statement to AFP.
'Thanat Suwannanont': Bernama's transliteration; Thai PBS and The Star also use 'Thanut Suvarnananda'. One spelling used throughout.
'Seventeen days before that': 14 Jul (Khaled) to 31 Jul (NSC) is 17 days.
General Consensus signatory for Malaysia was NSC secretary Mohammed Thajudeen (McDermott); 'Malaysia has facilitated since' is the document's own term ('act as facilitator').
source_notes: Incident count 22 Aug: ISOC final 51 (used); The Nation initial 25; FOCC4 preliminary 34. Suspension reason: Thanat (attack) and NSC (facilitator transition) both run, attributed. Cumulative death tolls deliberately off the cards (SBPAC 5,989 certified to Aug 2025 vs Deep South Watch 7,790; issue 2014 carries the certified figure). Rabin's appointment date: 1 Jul 2024 per MKN; an earlier search summary's '5 Jul 2025' was wrong. The Kelantan police 'no evidence' reply (2 Aug) and the Thai request to deny safe haven (27 Jul) are on issue 2014's cards and are not repeated here.
